thread:
Ava: Heads up — HelioMaps reported a surprise spike on their May dedicated invoice, ~$21,300 in burst charges on top of their reserved commit. They say they didn't run any big jobs. Invoice INV-20260507 attached. Can we reconcile?

Jonas: Got it. Can you send the customer_id and the usage export path? I can correlate meter IDs and model variants.

Ava: customer_id: helio-1234. Invoice PDF: https://invoices.redwood/INV-20260507.pdf. Billing export I pulled: s3://billing-exports/helio-1234/2026-05-01_2026-05-31.csv

billing-bot: Export ready — helio-1234/2026-05.csv (s3://billing-exports/helio-1234/2026-05.csv). Summary: total tokens billed 3.2B, burst tokens 210M, burst charges: $21,300.

Priya: Customer says they set a burst cap and expected overflow to be throttled. They shared a screenshot of their app usage that looks steady. Marcus, did CS see any telemetry from their account?

Marcus: I checked their app logs — they had a short surge on 2026-05-12 around 03:10–03:18 UTC but nothing ~21k worth. Filing #4521 with Helio to request their internal logs. They claim no internal test.

Jonas: I'm running the usage join now. Quick query I used:
```sql
SELECT timestamp, region, node_type, model, tags, tokens
FROM dedicated_usage
WHERE customer_id='helio-1234' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-05-01' AND '2026-05-31'
ORDER BY timestamp;
```
Found multiple rows where region=us-west-2 and node_type='p4d-highmem' during that window. Those requests are billed at higher per-token rate.

Ava: p4d-highmem? They have a small commit (2 GPUs reserved). Why would we run them on p4d? That sounds like a fallback/overflow to a higher-cost pool.

Jonas: Looks like autoscale policy allowed burst into an on-demand pool that is priced like p4d. Also found a tag on ~40% of the burst requests: `internal_test` — originated from an origin we normally mark as nonbillable (staging).

Priya: If part of this is internal/staging traffic we should definitely credit that. Also verify whether our autoscale policy incorrectly routed customer traffic to on-demand because of a capacity misreport.

Jonas: Agreed. Action items: 1) Mark the `internal_test` tagged requests as nonbillable and generate a corrected usage file. 2) Inspect scheduler logs for 2026-05-12 03:00–04:00 UTC for routing anomalies. I've opened an infra ticket: INF-7893.

billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-3307 to track HelioMaps invoice adjustment.

Marcus: FYI Helio is pushing for a quick fix; they said this overage is blocking procurement sign-off.

Ava: We need a proposal to send them. Rough math: If we remove `internal_test` traffic (~40% of burst tokens) that reduces burst charges to ~$12,780. If the remaining ~60% was due to routing into p4d instead of reserved pool, maybe offer a goodwill SLA credit for the portion caused by misrouting. Suggest we offer a credit of up to $10k while we finish the investigation. Thoughts?

Jonas: I can produce the corrected export by EOD and include flags: {internal_nonbillable, routed_to_on_demand}. If the routing error is confirmed, we should credit the on-demand differential, not full billed amount. I estimate differential ~$8,200.

Priya: From a customer retention POV, offering $10k credit (applied to next invoice) + an explanation and timeline sounds reasonable. We should get Finance sign-off first.

Ava: OK — authorization request: approve up to $10,000 credit to HelioMaps against INV-20260507 contingent on final reconciliation. Approvers: @Ava (Finance), @Jonas (Billing lead).

Jonas: I approve the plan and will attach the corrected CSV and routing evidence to BILL-3307 when ready.

Ava: Approved. I'll apply a provisional credit line now and annotate the invoice: "Provisional burst credit - under review" for $10,000 and schedule the final adjustment after INF-7893 completes. Marcus — please send Helio the note and expected timeline (48–72 hours).

Marcus: Will do. Draft message to customer: "We're investigating the unexpected burst charges. We've applied a provisional credit of $10,000 while we reconcile internal tags and routing. We'll follow up within 72 hours with the final breakdown and any additional credits if needed." Sending now. :white_check_mark:

billing-bot: BILL-3307 updated: provisional credit of $10,000 applied to INV-20260507. Support ticket linked: #4521.

Priya: Nice — keep me in the loop if Helio escalates to legal/procurement.

Jonas: I'll post the corrected usage CSV to s3://billing-exports/helio-1234/corrections/2026-05-corrected.csv and attach INF-7893 logs. ETA 6 hours.

Ava: Thanks everyone. If INF-7893 shows scheduler misreporting we'll do a retro credit and update capacity policies so this doesn't recur.

Marcus: Helio replied: "Appreciate the quick action — will hold payment pending your final reconciliation."

Ava: Marking thread for tracking. Last action: Jonas to upload artifacts, INF to confirm routing; Finance will finalize credits.

Jonas: Upload complete. s3://billing-exports/helio-1234/corrections/2026-05-corrected.csv; INF-7893 logs attached. Evidence: ~40% of burst rows tagged `internal_test` (flagged nonbillable). Remaining high-cost tokens were routed to on-demand due to transient capacity mismatch; differential calculated = $8,450.

Ava: Final resolution: apply provisional credit ($10,000) already done; now reconcile final numbers and issue additional credit $8,450 - $10,000 = \u2014 we owe them $8,450 but since we already applied $10,000, we'll refund the difference by reducing the credit? Wait — we applied too much. Actually provisional credit exceeded differential. We'll keep the $10,000 credit and add a small goodwill service credit of $500 for the customer experience, then close invoice. Net credit = $10,500. Approving net credit of $10,500.

Priya: Approved. I'll update the customer-facing note and close BILL-3307 once invoice reflects $10,500 credit.

billing-bot: BILL-3307 closed. Final credit applied: $10,500 to INV-20260507. Notification sent to helio-1234.

Marcus: Helio confirmed receipt and accepted the credit. Procurement moving forward. :tada:

Ava: Great — please add a post-mortem action to change autoscale routing policy and ensure internal/staging origins are never billed by default. INF-7893 -> PM-1022 for policy work.

Jonas: Added PM-1022. Closing from billing side.

Ava: Thanks team.
